title: Status progression + executive customer summary template
body:
Purpose: This is a concise, customer-facing executive summary template and an associated micro-update cadence for status page posts. Intended for incidents that affect inference correctness or latency for multi-tenant environments. Keep the language plain, action-focused, and short — customers want what happened, what we did, how we verified, and what they may need to do (if anything).

Key principles (brief):
- Micro-update cadence: three short updates spaced by objective checkpoints (initial acknowledgement, mitigation progress, and final verification/closure).
- Single-sentence TL;DR at top with measurable indicators (SLO impact window, percent of requests affected).
- Transparent but non-speculative root cause language; avoid internal playbook step details.
- Include a verification checklist customers can use to confirm restoration.

Suggested status page layout (130-300 words total):
1) Headline / TL;DR (1 sentence)
- Example: "TL;DR: We identified and mitigated a routing-induced model mismatch causing elevated error rates for text-generation requests between 2023-01-14 08:15–08:42 UTC; service returned to normal after staged rollback at 08:42 UTC."

2) Impact summary (1 short paragraph)
- What: brief description of symptoms (e.g., higher error rate, truncated streaming, stale embeddings).
- Who: percentage/estimation of tenants or percentage of requests affected (e.g., ~6% of requests or 3 enterprise tenants).
- Duration: start -> containment -> resolution timestamps in UTC.

3) Customer-facing root cause statement (1–2 sentences)
- High-level: e.g., "A configuration routing rule mismatch caused requests to be served by a model shard with incompatible kv-cache layout, producing assertion errors and increased tail latency."
- Avoid stack traces or playbook enumerations.

4) Mitigation actions taken (bulleted list)
- Immediate: circuit breakers, targeted routing to fallback model variant, redirecting traffic to EU region, temporary throttles for affected routes.
- Follow-up: canary rollback, cache reset, artifact verification, extended monitoring window.

5) Verification and evidence (short list)
- Automated checks we ran (synthetic requests, rank-stability test, embeddings checksum sampling).
- Customer verification steps (simple): e.g., 1) call /v1/health for tenant, 2) run quick prompt used in integration, 3) confirm latency and response shape match baseline.

6) Customer impact & recommended actions (1 paragraph + optional checklist)
- If action required: recommended steps (rotate keys if auth was involved; replay requests only if you opted into replay); otherwise: "No customer action required — your traffic is unaffected or was automatically reconciled."

7) Expected next update and closure content (1 sentence)
- When we’ll follow up: e.g., "We will post a full customer postmortem within 7 business days including timeline, root cause analysis, and corrective actions."

8) Contact & escalation
- Provide concise lines: Customer Success: cs-contacts@redwood.example; Dedicated customers: outline account rep + SE contact; Enterprise SRE escalation link with ticket reference.

Micro-update cadence (recommended timing and content):
- Update 1 (0–15 mins): Acknowledgement, short TL;DR, impacted routes, immediate mitigations in-flight.
- Update 2 (15–90 mins): Progress check with concrete indicators (percent traffic diverted, error-rate trend), ETA for next steps.
- Update 3 (closure): Final confirmation, short verification summary, link to postmortem draft and opt-in instructions for any customer replay/forensics.

Example customer executive summary (compact):
TL;DR: We detected elevated error rates and increased tail latency for text-generation requests routed through eu-west-1 between 2031-01-14 08:15–08:42 UTC; targeted routing rollback at 08:42 UTC restored expected behavior.
Impact: Approximately 5–7% of tenant requests experienced transient failures or truncated responses. No data loss detected; embedded outputs for affected calls were recomputed where necessary.
Root cause (high level): A routing policy change deployed in a dependent service caused a subset of requests to be sent to an incompatible model shard variant.
Mitigation: Immediately rolled back the deploy, routed affected traffic to a verified fallback model, and restarted a small set of serving nodes to clear inconsistent caches.
Verification: We validated restoration with synthetic end-to-end prompts (N=50) and continuous latency sampling for 30 minutes post-rollback. Customers can confirm by running their integration test prompt and verifying that response shape and latency align with pre-incident baselines.
Customer action: No action required unless you observe persistent incorrect outputs; contact your account rep for assistance.
Next steps: Full postmortem with timelines, RCA, and corrective measures will be published within 5 business days.

Customer-postmortem executive summary template (for inclusion in final postmortem):
- One-line incident summary.
- Impact metrics (requests affected, tenant count, duration).
- Root cause (executive-level).
- Timeline (UTC) with 5–7 key checkpoints.
- Customer-visible mitigations and verification evidence.
- Remediation & preventive actions (what we will change: rollout gate, extra preflight checks, adjustable routing policies, improved synthetic coverage).
- Open follow-ups and owner for each item (owner name + ETA).

Language tips and templates (short):
- Replace internal words like "rollback playbook" with "staged rollback".
- Use "we routed traffic to a verified fallback model" instead of naming internal model IDs.
- When offering replays: be explicit about consent, scope, and timeline (e.g., "If you opt in to a replay, we will reprocess only requests from your tenant between X and Y; opt-in window: 72 hours.").

Attachments checklist for closure post:
- Short timeline (CSV)
- Verification log snippets (anonymized)
- Opt-in replay form link (if applicable)
- Contact/EScalation card

Open questions / discussion notes for CS review:
- Do we want a standard opt-in form flow for replays across enterprise tiers?
- Should we publish a redacted sample verification log for customers to self-validate?
- Proposed metric: add "customer-visible recovery latency" to status page metadata for future incidents.

Notes to writer: keep final customer postmortem under 800–1200 words. Prioritize clear time-ordered checkpoints and an explicit verification section customers can use to confirm restoration. Avoid exposing internal runbook steps or PII.

Draft use cases: this template is good for: model fallback events, routing regressions, KV-cache corruption, streaming truncation events, and regional infra-induced tail-latency incidents.

End.
